notes.text: Yet — They cover all their wickedness with a profession of religion. Delight - There are many men who take some pleasure in knowing God's will and word, and yet do not conform their lives to it. As - As if they were a righteous people. Forsook - As if they were not guilty of any apostacy from God, or disobedience to God's precepts. Ask - As if they resolved to observe them. In approaching - In coming to my temple to hear my word, and to offer sacrifices.

Afflicted — Defrauded our appetites with fasting, of which this phrase is used, Levit xvi, 29. Ye find - Either you indulge yourselves in sensuality, as they did, chap. xxii, 13. But this does not agree with that afflicting of their souls which they now professed, and which God acknowledges; or you pursue and satisfy your own desires: though you abstain from bodily food, you do not mortify your sinful inclinations. Exact - Your money, got by your labour, and lent to others, either for their need or your own advantage, which you require either with usury, or at least with rigor, when either the general law of charity, or God's particular law, commanded the release, or at least the forbearance of them.

Behold — Your fasting days, wherein you ought in a special manner to implore the mercy of God, and to shew compassion to men, you employ in injuring or quarrelling with your brethren, your servants or debtors, or in contriving mischief against them. Heard - In strife and debate. By way of ostentation.

Chosen — Approve of, accept, or delight in, by a metonymy, because we delight in what we freely chuse. For a day - This may be understood, either for a man to take a certain time to afflict his soul in, and that either from even to even, Lev. xxiii, 32, or from morning to evening, or for a little time. Wilt thou call - Canst thou suppose it to be so? A fast - It being such an one as has nothing in it, but the dumb signs of a fast, nothing of deep humiliation appearing in it, or, real reformation proceeding from it. Acceptable day - A day that God will approve of.
The bands — The cruel obligations of usury and oppression.

Cast out — And thereby become wanderers, having no abiding place. To thy house - That thou be hospitable, and make thy house a shelter to them that have none of their own left. Hide not - That seek no occasion to excuse thyself. Thy own flesh - Some confine this to our own kindred; but we can look on no man, but there we contemplate our own flesh, and therefore it is barbarous, not only to tear, but not to love and succor him. Therefore feed him as thou wouldest feed thyself, or be fed; shelter him as thou wouldest shelter thyself, or be sheltered; clothe him as thou wouldest clothe thyself, or be clothed; if in any of these respects thou wert in his circumstances.

Thy light — Happiness and prosperity. Break forth - It shall not only appear, but break forth, dart itself forth, notwithstanding all difficulties, as the sun breaks, and pierces through a cloud. Thy health - Another metaphor to express the same thing. Righteousness - The reward of thy righteousness. Before thee - As the morning-star goes before the sun. The glory - His glorious power and providence. Thy rereward - Thus the angel of his presence secured the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt.

Answer — He will give an effectual demonstration, that he hears thee. Here l am - A phrase that notes a person to be ready at hand to help. Take away - From among you. The yoke - All those pressures and grievances before mentioned. Putting forth - Done by way of scoff, or disdainful insulting. Vanity - Any kind of evil words.

glossa.text:
*Cry.* ((HIER.)) The Lord to the prophets or to the apostles: the former chapter being ended, in which peace is announced to the just, and no rest to the wicked.

*As a trumpet.* ((ID.)) Where to the apostles, etc., *as far as* so let Israel, dead by sin, hear his own crimes.

*To my people.* As if he said: Let them see what a Father they have lost, who calls even sinners his people.

*As.* That is, why should I not hear them as I hear those who do justice in the Church, living justly and piously, confessing Christ true God and true man.

*They ask.* ((ID.)) Another rashness of the Jews, as though, trusting in a good conscience, they demand a just judgment, according to that: *Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence.*

*Why have we fasted.* They have forgotten the ancient history, that the Lord had no regard to the gifts of Cain, because he did not divide rightly with his brother, to whom he grudged charity towards God.

*Behold, in the day.* A fast acceptable to God is to abstain not only from foods, but from all unlawful things.

*You exact.* He who exacts from one who has not, does violence to God.
*Do not fast as until this day.* Lest he seem to reprove fasting, he teaches how one ought to fast.
*Is this such a fast.*
*The bundles.* ((ID.)) We understand sins, etc., *as far as* despise not the household of thy own seed.

*Break thy bread to the hungry.* ((ID.)) We break bread to the hungry, etc., *as far as* but the fullness of the soul.

*And thy own flesh.* ((ID.)) Recognize thy neighbour, in whatever need, as like to thyself, considering that thou art mortal and passible.

*Thy light.* As the morning light dissolves the darkness, so the light of truth puts errors to flight.

 *Justice.* Christ, who justifies all, shall go before unto glory.

*And the glory of the Lord shall gather thee up,* that is, shall receive thee to himself, who said: *Where I am, there also shall my minister be ((Joan. XII))*.
*To stretch out the finger.* To mark thy neighbours, to disparage them. That is, not only art thou not to think these things and not to do them, but thou art not even to disparage.

notes.text: Generation — The posterity.
Righteousness — The fruit or reward of his righteousness, which is God's blessing upon his estate.
Darkness — In the troubles and calamities of life. He - The upright man.

Lendeth — Gives freely to some, and lends to others according to the variety of their conditions. Affairs - His domestick affairs. Discretion - Not getting his estate unjustly, nor casting it away prodigally, nor yet withholding it from such as need it.
Moved — Though he may for a season be afflicted, yet he shall not be eternally destroyed.
Evil tidings — At the report of approaching calamities.

Dispersed — His goods, freely and liberally. Righteousness - His liberality, or the reward of it. Ever - What he gives is not lost, but indeed is the only part of his estate, which will abide with him to all eternity.

glossa.text: *Blessed is the man.* ((CASS.)) Here the Psalmist shows, after the deliverance, etc., *as far as* thirdly he affirms that adverse things befall the ungodly. *That feareth the Lord.* The fear of the world makes men wretched, but the fear of God makes a man desire those things whereby he is blessed. *In the commandments.* This the fear of God does, that he should will. And he says not "he shall do," etc., *as far as* and *the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things.*

*Mighty.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Behold the rewards of that blessed man. *His seed.* That is, the reward of a good work; *Shall be mighty upon earth,* not upon this earth, where he is a laughing-stock, but upon the heavenly. Or even here in this present time, wherein it is less seen. *Seed,* the works of mercy, whence comes the everlasting harvest. *Mighty,* because with a very small thing, even as with a great one, the kingdom of heaven is bought. *The generation.* Not of the flesh, but of imitation. Or the works of the upright. *The upright* are they who resist not the Father when he corrects, and who believe him when he promises, and who believe not that their works have perished when no requital is made them in time. For there are those who do those good things while hoping here for a reward from God, or wishing to please men, which is not the blessed man: and yet,

*Glory and wealth in his house.* That is, in the secret of the heart, where he dwells with the hope of eternal life, where holy riches and eternal glory are laid up. *Justice.* This is his glory, these are his riches, which nevertheless he has from God. *It remaineth for ever.* As it were, he is not blessed for a time.
*There hath risen up.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he treats of the coming of the Lord, etc., *as far as* that he may fortify it beforehand with firm allegations and assertions in the judgment. Or,
*He sheweth mercy.* ((ID.)) He who gives to the needy; *He lendeth,* he who grants a loan, to receive afterwards as much again.

*His heart is ready to hope in the Lord, his heart is strengthened, it remaineth,* etc. ((AUG.)) It is plain therefore that this man seeks not his own things, but the things which are Christ's; he bears labours patiently, he awaits the promises with confidence. ((CASS.)) Or, if any man threatens evils, he fears not, but is ready.

*He hath distributed.* He hopes not to fear, because he has distributed. *He hath given to the poor.* ((AUG.)) Behold, this man was buying what he did not see, but that other was keeping a treasure for him in heaven, who vouchsafes to hunger and to thirst in the poor upon earth. *His justice remaineth for ever and ever.* ((CASS.)) He gave what was his own, and lived justly and godly; or, he who gives what is his own works justice. *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* Because he is humble here, there he shall have power.

notes.text: And I accordingly came to you, not with loftiness of speech or of wisdom — I did not affect either deep wisdom or eloquence. Declaring the testimony of God - What God gave me to testify concerning his Son.

I determined not to know anything — To wave all my other knowledge, and not to preach anything, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified - That is, what he did, suffered, taught. A part is put for the whole.
And I was with you — At my first entrance. In weakness - Of body, 2 Cor. xii, 7 And in fear - Lest I should offend any. And in much trembling - The emotion of my mind affecting my very body.

And my speech in private, as well as my public preaching, was not with the persuasive words of human wisdom, such as the wise men of the world use; but with the demonstration of the Spirit and of power — With that powerful kind of demonstration, which flows from the Holy Spirit; which works on the conscience with the most convincing light, and the most persuasive evidence.
That your faith might not be built on the wisdom or power of man, but on the wisdom and power of God.

Yet we speak wisdom — Yea, the truest and most excellent wisdom. Among the perfect - Adult, experienced Christians. By wisdom here he seems to mean, not the whole Christian doctrine, but the most sublime and abstruse parts of it. But not the wisdom admired and taught by the men of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, Jewish or heathen, that come to nought - Both they and their wisdom, and the world itself.

But we speak the mysterious wisdom of God, which was hidden for many ages from all the world, and is still hidden even from "babes in Christ;" much more from all unbelievers. Which God ordained before the world — So far is this from coming to nought, like worldly wisdom. For our glory - Arising from the glory of our Lord, and then to be revealed when all worldly glory vanishes.

Had they known it — That wisdom. They would not have crucified - Punished as a slave. The Lord of glory - The giving Christ this august title, peculiar to the great Jehovah, plainly shows him to be the supreme God. In like manner the Father is styled, "the Father of glory," Eph. i, 17; and the Holy Ghost, "the Spirit of glory," 1 Pet. iv, 14. The application of this title to all the three, shows that the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are "the God of glory;" as the only true God is called, Psalm xxix, 3, and Acts vii, 2.

But this ignorance of theirs fulfils what is written concerning the blessings of the Messiah's kingdom. No natural man hath either seen, heard, or known, the things which God hath prepared, saith the prophet, for them that love him. Isaiah lxiv, 4

But God hath revealed — Yea, and "freely given," ver. 12. Them to us - Even inconceivable peace, and joy unspeakable. By his Spirit - Who intimately and fully knows them. For the Spirit searcheth even the deep things of God - Be they ever so hidden and mysterious; the depths both of his nature and his kingdom.

For what man knoweth the things of a man — All the inmost recesses of his mind; although men are all of one nature, and so may the more easily know one another. So the things of God knoweth no one but the Spirit - Who, consequently, is God.
Now we have received, not the spirit of the world — This spirit is not properly received; for the men of the world always had it. But Christians receive the Spirit of God, which before they had not.

glossa.text: *For I judged not myself to know anything.* He who speaks higher things to one less capable works not profit, but the display of himself.
*The perfect.* Not those who already know and are teachers, who have no need of it, but hearers now capable.

*In a mystery.* By expounding the mysteries of the Old Testament in which Christ was signified, as in the sacrifice of Abel, or of Abraham. *Which is hidden.* Because it is not in words, but in power: not comprehensible by human reason, but credible by the efficacy of the Spirit.
*For if they had known.* Either the lesser, that he was the Messiah promised in the law, or the greater, that he was God, or the Son of God: *they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.*

*Nor into the heart of man.* Below the heart of man is that which ascends into the heart; above the heart is that eternal thing to which the heart ascends. Or it is not man, but the spirit, that knows. *Hath ascended.* A thing is said to ascend in the heart when, being well understood, it pleases.

*Searcheth,* etc. The Spirit of God is said to search all things, not that he may find what he does not know, but because he leaves nothing at all that he does not know, or because he makes thee search; for what thou doest by his gift, he is said to do, because without him thou wouldst not do it.

*But the Spirit that is of God.* The Holy Spirit is assuredly of the Father and of the Son, and ours as well. For what has been given is referred both to him who gave, and to those to whom he gave. And so the Holy Spirit is not only of the Father and of the Son, who gave, but is also ours, who received. And this is not that spirit of ours in which we are: because that very spirit of ours in which we are is itself the spirit of man, which is in him. And yet we have received that very spirit also which is man's. But one thing is what we receive, that we might be, another what we received, that we might be holy. But the spirit of man is taken in Scripture for the soul itself, or for the rational power of the soul itself. For he gave us nature that we might be, a soul that we might live, a mind that we might understand. *That we may know.* Many have the gifts of God, and by not knowing from whom they have them, they are puffed up with impious vanity. No one is blessed by the gifts of God who is ungrateful to the giver, whence in the Gospel: *He that hath, to him shall be given.* To have fully is to know whence one has it. *He therefore that hath not,* that is, he who knows not whence he has it, *even that which he hath shall be taken away from him ((Luc. VIII))* .

notes.text: Ye — Not the apostles, not ministers only; but all ye who are thus holy, are the salt of the earth - Are to season others. Mark ix, 50; Luke xiv, 34.

Ye are the light of the world — If ye are thus holy, you can no more be hid than the sun in the firmament: no more than a city on a mountain - Probably pointing to that on the brow of the opposite hill.
Nay, the very design of God in giving you this light was, that it might shine. Mark iv, 21; Luke viii, 16; xi, 33.
That they may see — and glorify - That is, that seeing your good works, they may be moved to love and serve God likewise.

Think not — Do not imagine, fear, hope, that I am come - Like your teachers, to destroy the law or the prophets. I am not come to destroy - The moral law, but to fulfil - To establish, illustrate, and explain its highest meaning, both by my life and doctrine.

Till all things shall be effected — Which it either requires or foretells. For the law has its effect, when the rewards are given, and the punishments annexed to it inflicted, as well as when its precepts are obeyed. Luke xvi, 17; xxi, 33.
One of the least — So accounted by men; and shall teach - Either by word or example; shall be the least - That is, shall have no part therein.
The righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees — Described in the sequel of this discourse.

glossa.text:
*You are the salt of the earth.* Here now is shown the office of the apostles, namely that they are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. This belongs especially to the apostles, who ought to be adorned with the aforesaid virtues, namely poverty and the rest, that they may be the best salt, seasoning others by doctrine and by the example of their own life. Salt, health from corruption. Whence the prophet: *I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the ends of the earth.* 

*But if the salt,* etc. That is, if you, by whom others are to be seasoned, give way before adverse or prosperous things: by whom shall error be taken away from you, when God has chosen to raise you up for others? It is good for nothing: because (as another evangelist says) it is useful neither to the earth, which by being cast upon it it hinders from sprouting, nor to the dunghill, which it does not suffer to grow fruitful. So he who goes backward neither bears fruit himself, nor is able to till others, but is cast out of the Church, and is laughed at in these words: *This man began to build, and was not able to finish. If the salt shall lose its savor ((Luc. IV))*. That is, if through fear or through greed the teacher has let go the savor of wisdom, by whom shall his foolishness be amended? This befits the apostles alone: what follows befits all masters: *It is good for nothing any more,* etc. At the end he concludes thus concerning all: *Unless your righteousness abound,* etc.

*And be trodden upon by men.* The holy and true minister of Christ, even if he is laughed at by the wicked, cannot be trodden upon, because fixed in mind he remains in heaven.

*You are the light of the world.* Salt before light, because life before doctrine: life leads to the knowledge of truth. He who fears God does not lack knowledge.

*The light of the world.* There is another cause why they ought not to fail: because they are enlightened by Christ in word and in example: wherever they are carried among worldly men they ought to minister the light of faith and of knowledge. And as (because they are salt) they ought to drive away corruption: so also they ought to put darkness (because they are light) to flight.

*A city cannot,* etc. Because the apostles are foundations, they are fitly called a city. *Upon a mountain.* The place hints at the mountain of righteousness, which is lofty, whereby you are made public so that you may not hide yourselves. For there is no power of slipping away or of doing anything in secret; therefore rule your subjects mercifully within by counsel, and without against adversaries defend them by fighting for righteousness: which belongs to the spirit of counsel and of fortitude.

*Neither do they light a lamp.* By household examples he teaches them not to hide the light of the word committed to them. They do not light, that is, the doctrine of preaching was not given for this, that they should hide it and subject it to the servitude of the body, while they fear certain things. But let them subject their body to the ministry of God, that through the voice and the other offices of the body the light may appear more excellent than the rest. Whence it is said ((I Cor. IX)): *I chastise my body,* etc. Or, Christ lit a lamp, when he filled the earthen shell of human nature with the flame of his divinity: which he neither hid from believers, nor shut up under a bushel, that is, the measure of the law, or within the bounds of a single nation. But upon the candlestick, that is, the Church, he fastened the faith of his incarnation, where all can behold it who are in the house, that is, in the Church, or in the world. Whence he adds: *So let your light shine,* etc. *A candlestick.* As Christ is the lamp, the candlestick is the cross, upon which he was to be lifted up. The candlestick is the Church, which bears the word of the present life.

*So let your light shine,* etc. And do all these things in such a way that you do not set the end of your good work in the praises of men. *That they may see,* etc. I require works, that they may be seen, and that so the doctrine may be confirmed: and this not to your own glory.

*Do not think.* After he had exhorted them to suffer all things for the truth, and not to hide it, and to work the glory of God, he begins to teach what they are to teach. As if he were saying: What is this that thou forbiddest to be hidden, for which thou biddest all things to be suffered? is there anything against the law? *I am not come to destroy the law, but to fulfil,* either by doing what it says, or by supplying what was lacking and imperfect.

*One jot. ((BEDA.))* Here it is shown that the things which are thought least in the law are full of spiritual sacraments, and all things, etc., *as far as* because the jot signifies ten, that is, the decalogue, whose apex is the perfection of the Gospel.

*All things be fulfilled.* Let them be spiritually fulfilled, or let the imperfect be perfected, and let the things that signify be consummated, that is, by the fulfilment.


[0092D]

*He therefore that shall break,* etc. The least things are the cross of Christ and his passion, and he who is ashamed of them is least; he who confesses them is great. Or he marks the Pharisees, who let go the commandments of God for their own traditions, which are worth nothing, while they pass over even the least thing that is in the law. But morally he breaks it who does not fulfil it, but holds it as these things were given to the weak. Or he who does not understand it spiritually. To break, is not to do what one rightly understands, or not to understand what one does not distort, or to lessen the wholeness of Christ's superadding.

*He shall be called the least,* etc. In the kingdom of heaven he shall be called least who will be unworthy in it, in which there is none least but all are great.

 *But he that shall do.* He who shall not break it, and so teaches, is not least, yet not great: but he does what he teaches. *For only the doers of the law are just before God ((Rom. II))*.

*But I say to you.* When he says, I say, he struck in a great force and a deep understanding for thinking: he shows how he superadds. And he does not undo the things he had commanded before. It is even more to love enemies than not to hate them: not to covet, than not to commit adultery: not to be angry, than not to kill.

*Unless,* etc. That is, you shall fulfil not only the least precepts of the law, but also those which I add: because while the things added are done unto perfection, these too are more fully performed which were set down before unto a beginning: because he who does not look upon a woman to lust after her, neither does he commit fornication: nor does he kill who is not angry.

*Your righteousness.* He calls the righteousness of the Pharisees all those things actually commanded for the worship of God: or the mystical things of the figures, established only according to the letter.

registers.label: Spare
lines: You are the salt of the earth.
You are the light of the world.
Share your bread; loose the bonds of the oppressed.
Then our light shall break forth like the dawn.
Let your light shine before others.
That they may give glory to God.
Come, let us worship the God who lights us.
Let our light shine. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: This is the fast God is after: not bowed heads and empty bellies, but bread broken for the hungry and the chains struck off the bound.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
Do that, says the prophet, and your light will break out like the morning, and your healing will spring up quick.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
You are salt, Jesus says, so do not lose your savor; you are a city on a hill that cannot be hidden.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
So do not hide the lamp under a basket; set it high, and let the whole house fill with light.
Let your light break forth like the dawn. Thanks be to God!
